note: The rate card: Egma's price for one unit of one provider's work, one entry
per model in the executable catalog beside this file.
A price is never edited. A change is a new entry with a later
effectiveFrom, and rating picks the newest entry effective at or before
the usage's own instant — so a past simulation's cost never moves and this
file's history is the price history.
usdPerMillion is US dollars per 1,000,000 of the unit named beside it, as a
decimal string so no float rounds it on the way in. It is written per
million because that is how the providers publish token prices, and because
one micro-dollar is exactly one unit at $1.00 per million — so a record's
amount in micros is quantity times this number, with no scale factor to get
source is the page the number was read from and readAt the day it was read.

Published as "$0.017 / minute" with no token price at all, so the billed unit is the audio's own duration. Per million seconds: 0.017 / 60 * 1000000 = 283.333333333333, carried to twelve decimal places because a sixtieth of a cent does not terminate.
Published as "$0.017 / minute", converted per second exactly as gpt-live-transcribe's entry sets out.

Token-billed: the pricing table publishes one Input column ($2.50) and one Output column ($10.00), and the realtime transcription event splits its input into audio and text tokens under that one input price. The "$0.006 / minute" beside them is the page's own estimate, not the billed unit.

Token-billed on the same shape as gpt-4o-transcribe: one published Input column ($1.25) covering audio and text input tokens, one Output column ($5.00). The "$0.003 / minute" beside them is the page's own estimate.

Nova-3 streaming, monolingual, pay-as-you-go: "Current price $0.0048/min" (the same row shows "Regular price $0.0077/min"). The published pay-as-you-go price is the base rate, per the rate-card rule. Per million seconds: 0.0048 / 60 * 1000000 = 80.

Cartesia publishes credits, not dollars: ink-2 costs "3 credits per second of audio". Cartesia publishes no pay-as-you-go dollar price, only plans, so the base rate is the published rate of its smallest paid plan — Pro, $5 per month for 100K credits, which is $50 per 1M credits (https://cartesia.ai/pricing, read 2026-09-07). 3 credits per second at $50 per 1M credits is $150 per 1M seconds.

"Standard TTS costs approximately 1 credit per character." Cartesia publishes no pay-as-you-go dollar price, only plans, so the base rate is the published rate of its smallest paid plan — Pro, $5 per month for 100K credits, which is $50 per 1M credits (https://cartesia.ai/pricing, read 2026-09-07). 1 credit per character therefore prices at $50 per 1M characters. Cartesia's own "approximately" is its transcript pre-processing: the credits it counts can differ slightly from the characters Egma sent.
The same credit meter as sonic-3.5 — one credit per character, priced at the smallest paid plan's published $50 per 1M credits, on the ruling written into that entry.
Published directly in the unit Egma measures: "$15.00 / 1M characters".
Published directly in the unit Egma measures: "$30.00 / 1M characters".

AN APPROXIMATION, and the only one in this file. OpenAI bills this model by audio output token ($12.00 per 1M audio tokens); Egma measures the characters it sent, and OpenAI publishes no character price and no per-minute estimate for it (its Estimated cost cell is empty). Derived from OpenAI's own numbers in two steps. (1) OpenAI's audio-token rate, from its transcription rows on the same page: $0.006 per minute at $2.50 per 1M audio tokens is 2,400 audio tokens per minute, and the mini row agrees exactly ($0.003 at $1.25 per 1M). So $12.00 per 1M audio tokens is $0.0288 per minute of generated audio. (2) Characters per minute of speech: Cartesia publishes "One minute of audio generation requires 750-800 credits" at approximately one credit per character (https://cartesia.ai/pricing, read 2026-09-07); 750 is the end that does not under-price. $0.0288 / 750 = $0.0000384 per character, i.e. $38.40 per 1M characters — equivalently 3.2 audio tokens per character. Replace this with a published price the day OpenAI publishes one.
